project.objective: Who were the maternal grandparents of Jimmie Jewel Neal (born 10 July 1884 in Hillsboro, Hill, Texas, died 7 March 1938 in Carlsbad, Eddy, New Mexico)?

questions.question: Who was Jimmie Jewel Neal's mother, as documented by primary source records for Jimmie Jewel Neal (born 10 July 1884, Hillsboro, Hill County, Texas; died 7 March 1938, Carlsbad, Eddy County, New Mexico)?
questions.rationale: Martha J Wood appears in the tree as Jimmie's mother, but no source citations exist. The research objective — identifying Jimmie's maternal grandparents — depends first on confirming from primary records (death certificate, census, birth records) who Jimmie's mother was. Texas death records (1938) and federal census records (1880–1910) are strong candidates. This is the gatekeeper question: its answer names the woman whose parents are the objective.

questions.question: Who were the parents of Martha J (born approximately 1858–1859 in Georgia; previously Mrs. Landham; married James M. Neal in Hill County, Texas on 31 July 1879; died 30 May 1906 in Files Valley, Hill County, Texas; tree person LKYG-VKB) — the maternal grandmother of Jimmie Jewel Neal?
questions.rationale: With q_001 resolved at probable (Martha J, formerly Mrs. Landham then Mrs. Neal then Mrs. Hamby, is Jimmie Jewel Neal's biological mother), the research objective now requires identifying Martha J's parents — Jimmie's maternal grandparents. Martha was born approximately 1858–1859 in Georgia (1900 census) and migrated to Texas before 1879. Her maiden name is not yet confirmed from primary records; the tree attributes 'Wood' but the specific Wood family has not been identified. The most productive records are: (1) the 1880 Hill County TX census which should find Martha J as wife of James M. Neal and may show her precise age; (2) Texas marriage records for the prior Lanham/Landham marriage (which may name her maiden name and possibly parents); and (3) Georgia 1860/1870 census searches for her birth family. This is the gatekeeper question for the research objective.

items.rationale: Jimmie Jewel Neal died 7 March 1938 in Carlsbad, Eddy County, NM. New Mexico death certificates from this era include the decedent's parents' names — directly answering who her mother was. FamilySearch holds the 1938 Eddy County death certificate volume (imageGroupNumber 004229757, 2,587 images, 97% indexed + full-text). Collections: New Mexico, County Death Records, 1907-1952 (id 1966081) and New Mexico, Deaths, 1889-1945 (id 1546466). Highest-priority source — a single search should retrieve the certificate.

Jimmie Neal (born 10 July 1884) would be approximately 15-16 years old in June 1900 and almost certainly living in her parents' household in Hill County, TX. The federal census names every household member and their relationship to the head — establishing her mother's name directly. Hill County 1900 census is 96-98% indexed on FamilySearch (vols. 004118499_001 and 004118498_003). Martha J Wood and James Monroe Neal are in the tree as unsourced parents; this census will confirm or correct their names and ages.

Jimmie was not yet born in June 1880 (she was born July 1884), but her parents — the Neal family — would appear in Hill County. Locating the family in 1880 establishes their names, ages, and birthplaces before Jimmie's birth, serving as verification of identities found in the 1900 census. The 1880 federal census is indexed + images on FamilySearch. Searching under 'Neal' in Hill County should locate the household if they were already settled there.

A marriage record for James Monroe Neal and Martha J Wood (or whoever Jimmie's parents prove to be) confirms the couple as a unit and — critically — supplies the mother's maiden name, which census and death records typically omit for married women. Hill County marriage records 1873-1937 are 100% indexed on FamilySearch across multiple volumes (vols. 004820309, 004820303-004820310, 004820617, etc.). Per the localities entry loc_001, Hill County marriage records are an exceptional strength of this jurisdiction. Even if the mother is confirmed by the death certificate, her maiden name still requires this source.

By 1910 Jimmie would be approximately 25-26 years old and may already have been living in Eddy County, NM (where she died in 1938). If her parents also moved to NM, they may appear with or near her. The 1910 federal census is nationally indexed + images on FamilySearch. Search both Hill County TX and Eddy County NM to bracket the family's likely migration window from Texas to New Mexico.

Jimmie died in Carlsbad in March 1938, so she was resident in Eddy County in 1930 (age ~46). The 1930 census may show her household and — if her mother was still living — could place her mother with or near Jimmie. The 1930 federal census is nationally indexed + images on FamilySearch.

Hill County maintained county-level birth registers from 1870, predating Texas state civil registration (1903). Jimmie's 10 July 1884 birth may be recorded with her mother's name. FamilySearch vol. 008992082 (886 images, full-text searchable, 0% name-indexed) and delayed birth records vol. 008152748 (5,414 images, full-text searchable) and index vol. 008413381 cover this period. Per localities entry loc_001, full-text search on 'Neal' should surface a birth record if one was filed. Also check the general birth index vol. 008502334.

A published obituary for Jimmie Jewel Neal in the Carlsbad Current-Argus or other local paper in March 1938 would likely name her surviving family — including her mother (if living) or identify her as a daughter of named individuals. Obituaries often record maternal family relationships that no other source captures. This is the FAN-directed item per BCG Standard 14. Search via Chronicling America (LOC), GenealogyBank, and the New Mexico State Library. The Carlsbad Current-Argus is the primary local paper for this area and period.

If Jimmie's parents (James Monroe Neal and/or Martha J Wood) died in Texas after 1903, their Texas death certificates would name their own parents — supplying Jimmie's maternal grandparents and confirming the identity of her mother. Ancestry holds 'Texas Death Certificates, 1903-1982' (collection 2272); FamilySearch also holds Texas Deaths, 1890-1977 (collection 1983324). Invoked as a fallback if pli_001 (Jimmie's NM death cert) is illegible, unavailable, or omits the parents' names.

Martha J married James M. Neal in Hill County TX on 31 July 1879. The 1880 census (enumerated June 1880) should capture them as a recently married couple in Hill County TX. This record would give Martha's precise age (confirming her birth year ~1858-1860) and, critically, her birthplace at the county/state level in Georgia if reported. The 1880 census also records parents' birthplaces for each person, which may provide geographic leads for her birth family. loc_001 confirms Hill County TX 1880 census records are indexed on FamilySearch (collection 1417683). Highest priority — most likely to be found and most informative for narrowing the search.

Martha J was a widow (styled 'Mrs Mattie Landham') when she married James M. Neal in 1879, meaning she had a prior marriage to a man named Lanham/Landham. The Smith County TX marriage register (FamilySearch vols. 007255720 [1857-1876] and 007255721 [1875-1889]) is 100% indexed and fulltext-searchable (loc_004). Searching for all Lanham, Landham, and Wood marriages in Smith County 1865-1879 may identify: (a) Martha's own prior marriage to a Lanham man (with her maiden name), or (b) a Wood family member's marriage that corroborates her maiden name. The 1869 W F Lanham / M J Wood marriage is already known (log_022); searching for additional Lanham-Wood matches in the 1870s (vol. 007255721) may reveal Martha's own marriage. Her maiden name and parents would likely appear on the marriage register if it follows the standard Texas form.

Martha J was born approximately 1858-1859 in Georgia (1900 census, a_049). Her maiden name may be Wood (per tree attribution, not yet confirmed from primary records). The 1860 US Census is the single highest-value search for her birth family: Martha would appear as an infant/toddler in her parents' household. A Georgia-wide search for households named Wood with a daughter born 1856-1862 should surface a small number of candidates. The parents' names and ages, and the county, would then anchor the follow-on searches. loc_003 confirms the 1860 census is fully indexed on FamilySearch. If maiden name is not Wood, the 1880 Hill County TX census (pli_010) may supply a more precise birthplace to narrow the Georgia search.

The 1869 Lanham-Wood marriage in Smith County TX suggests the Wood family had a presence in or connection to Smith County by January 1869. The 1870 US Census (enumerated June 1870, six months after the Lanham-Wood marriage) may show: (a) W F Lanham with his wife M J Lanham (née Wood) and her Wood family connections; (b) a Wood family in Smith County who brought Martha from Georgia. loc_004 confirms the Smith County 1870 census is 96% indexed on FamilySearch (vol. 004267896). A search for Wood households in Smith County 1870 will test whether the Wood family was present in northeast Texas by that date. Also search for 'Lanham' in Smith County 1870 to find the Lanham household after the January 1869 marriage.

If the Wood birth family is not found in the 1860 census or if they emigrated to Texas between 1860 and 1870, searching the 1870 Georgia census may show them in Georgia before any emigration. Alternatively, if they had already moved to Texas by 1870, the 1870 census may show only younger siblings (if any) remaining in Georgia. Fallback for the 1860 Georgia search (pli_012). loc_003 confirms the 1870 Georgia census is fully indexed.

Georgia Tax Digests 1787-1900 (FamilySearch col. 4130006, 2.88M records) are indexed and list taxable heads of household annually. If the Wood birth family is located in a specific Georgia county via the 1860 census, the tax digests can track them in non-census years (1857-1859, 1861-1869) and confirm county of residence. This is especially valuable given Georgia courthouse fires during Sherman's March (1864-65). The tax digests often survive courthouse fires. loc_003 notes this is the most powerful record for locating a family between census years in Georgia.

Georgia County Marriages 1785-1950 (FamilySearch col. 1927197, 1.9M records) provide indexed access to parents' marriage records. Once the Georgia county is identified (from the 1860 census or tax digests), the parents' marriage record should name both partners and supply their ages and parentage if the register followed the full-form style. The marriage likely falls in the 1840s-early 1850s (parents born ~1825-1840 to have a daughter in 1858-1859). This is the parents' marriage record as a distinct item from the general Georgia census searches. loc_003 confirms good coverage.

FAN/contextual item. Georgia Probate Records 1742-1990 (FamilySearch col. 1999178, 203K records) include wills and estate administrations. If Martha's father died during or after the Civil War, a probate record may name his wife and all minor children (including Martha J), giving her exact age, her mother's name, and potentially other siblings. Widow's pension applications (Confederate Service/Pension col. 3038333) from the same era are also valuable if the father served in the Confederate Army. loc_003 flags these as critical if the father died before 1875.

Martha J (LKYG-VKB) was in Hill County TX by 1879. If her family migrated from Georgia to Hill County TX by 1870, she would appear (~10 years old) as a daughter in a Wood household. This is the most direct search for her parents. Hill County TX 1870 census is indexed on FamilySearch.

Martha J was a widow named 'Mattie Landham' when she married James M. Neal on 31 July 1879 in Hill County TX. Her first marriage to Mr. Landham must have occurred ~1875-1879 (she was born ~1859). A Hill County TX marriage record for a Landham/Lanham groom marrying a Wood or other bride would confirm Martha's maiden name and potentially name her parents.

W F Lanham married M J Wood in Smith County TX on 7 January 1869. The couple should appear in the June 1870 census but were not in Smith County. A statewide Texas search for W F Lanham in 1870 would locate the couple and reveal M J Wood Lanham's birth year and state — confirming whether she can be identified with Martha J (LKYG-VKB, born ~1859 GA). If M J Wood Lanham was born significantly earlier than 1859, she is a different person; if near 1859 and born in Georgia, she may be Martha with an underestimated birth year.

Joseph B Wood (born 1836 GA) had daughter Martha J Wood (born 1860 GA) in Whitfield County GA in 1870. If the family migrated to Texas between 1870 and 1880, they may appear in Texas 1880 census. Martha J herself would be absent (married Landham ~1875-1878, then Neal July 1879) but the remaining family (Joseph B, wife Mary E, younger children) would appear. Confirming migration to Texas would strengthen the identification of Martha J Wood (Whitfield County GA) with LKYG-VKB.

Foranes (Clerk, County Court of Smith County). Return of solemnization: 'I joined in Marriage as Husband & Wife W. F. Lanham and M. J. Wood on The 7 day of January A.D. 1869,' signed by R. Carlton, J.P. Filed in office January 13th 1869. Adjacent entry No. 157 (Stephens/Burns) also shows 1869 throughout. Georgia County Marriages 1785-1950 search for Joseph Wood marrying Mary, 1850-1862. 11 results examined. KEY PARTIAL MATCH: ark:/61903/1:1:KXV8-2V1 — 'J. B. Wood' married 'Molly J. Blackman' on 17 November 1859 in Fulton County, GA. 'Molly' is a well-established nickname for 'Mary'; 'J. B.' matches 'Joseph B.' perfectly. Timing is consistent: marriage Nov 1859, first child Martha J. born ~1860 (nine months later). DISCREPANCY: bride's middle initial is 'J.' (Molly J.) while the 1870 census shows wife as 'Mary E. Wood' — the middle initials differ (J vs E). This could be a recording variation, a different middle name used in different contexts, or (less likely) a different family. No other Joseph B. Wood / Mary E. Wood marriage found. The Fulton County location (Atlanta area) is ~90 miles from Whitfield County (1870 residence), which is unusual but not impossible — the family may have relocated between 1859 and 1870. CONCLUSION: possible corroborating evidence, but the middle initial discrepancy prevents a confident identification of the bride as Mary E. Wood of the 1870 census. Will note in proof narrative as supporting-but-uncertain record."

Household members: (head, male, born 1806 GA — no given name indexed), Mary N Wood (female, born 1833 GA), Benjamin D Wood (male, born 1868 GA), Babe Wood (male, born 1870 GA). NO Martha J. Wife 'Mary N' (born 1833 GA) does NOT match Joshua's wife Stacy (born ~1812 SC). This is a DIFFERENT family, not Joshua Wood's household. CONCLUSION: MC3C-64S eliminates itself as Joshua Wood's 1870 household. Joshua Wood (born ~1805 SC, last seen Jackson County GA 1860) cannot be located in Jackson County GA in 1870, and NO Martha J. born ~1860 appears in any Jackson County GA household across all searches. The competing parentage candidate (Joshua Wood as potential father of Martha J.) has NO positive evidence supporting it — no Martha J. ever found in Joshua Wood's household in any census year — and is hereby ruled out.

## Research Question

Who was Jimmie Jewel Neal’s mother, as documented by primary source records for Jimmie Jewel Neal (born 10 July 1884, Hillsboro, Hill County, Texas; died 7 March 1938, Carlsbad, Eddy County, New Mexico)?

## Conclusion

**Martha J (formerly Mrs. Landham, then Mrs. Neal, then Mrs. Hamby) — tree person LKYG-VKB, born approximately August 1859 in Georgia, died 30 May 1906 in Files Valley, Hill County, Texas — was Jimmie Jewel Neal’s biological mother at the GPS probable confidence level. Her maiden name has not been confirmed from primary records consulted in this phase.**

## Evidence

### Hill County, Texas Marriage Record, 31 July 1879 (direct evidence of the Neal marriage)

The Hill County marriage register records the marriage of **James M. Neal (Mr)** and **Mattie Landham (Mrs)** on 31 July 1879, licensed 30 July 1879, officiated by James Leauphill, Baptist Minister (src_006). The ‘Mrs’ honorific explicitly identifies the bride as a widow: she was previously married to a man named Lanham/Landham (a_136). ‘Mattie’ is a standard 19th-century nickname for Martha (a_134).

This marriage (31 Jul 1879) predates the births of both Neal children: Claudie Neal (born September 1882) and Jimmie Jewel Neal (born 10 July 1884) by 2–4 years. The timeline is consistent with both children being born within this Neal marriage, making Martha J (formerly Mrs. Landham) the biological mother (a_137).

### 1900 United States Census, Hill County, Texas (primary indirect evidence)

The 1900 federal census for Justice Precinct 2, Hill County, Texas enumerated the William S. Hamby household (src_004). Two Neal-surnamed children appear as **stepchildren** of head William S. Hamby:

- **Claudie Neal** (step_child_1): Female, born September 1882, Texas — listed as stepdaughter (a_083)
- **James Neal** (step_child_2 = Jimmie Jewel Neal, KNXW-M3T): Born July 1884, Texas — listed as stepson (a_092); the enumerator rendered ‘Jimmie’ as the male name ‘James,’ a common transcription error

The wife of head William S. Hamby is **Martha J Hamby** (a_047): born August 1859 in Georgia (a_049–a_050), married to Hamby approximately 1888 (a_054). Her 1888 Hamby marriage postdates the births of both Neal children, establishing those children were born during a prior Neal marriage.

The **stepchild inference** (a_093): The census encodes the Neal children as stepchildren of the *head* William S. Hamby. The Neal children carry the surname Neal, not Hamby. Since Martha J is the wife and mother of the Hamby biological children, the step-encoding implies Martha J is the Neal children’s biological mother from her prior Neal marriage. The alternative — that the Neal children were William’s by a prior marriage — is contradicted by the census: his biological children would be encoded as ‘son’ and ‘daughter,’ not ‘stepchildren.’

### 1910 United States Census, Cottle County, Texas (corroboration)

The 1910 federal census again enumerated the William S. Hamby household (src_005). By 1910 Martha J had died (William is widowed, a_104; consistent with Find a Grave death date of 30 May 1906). **Jewell Warn** appears as **step-daughter** of the now-widowed William S. Hamby (a_120). This is Jimmie Jewel Neal: female (a_115), born approximately 1885 Texas (a_117), widowed (a_118), with children Neal Warn (born ~1905 TX) and Herby Warn (born ~1908 TX). The step-daughter relationship is independently encoded in a separate enumeration by a different enumerator 10 years after the 1900 census, after Martha J’s death.

### Negative evidence

Jimmie Jewel Neal Yarbro’s 1938 New Mexico death certificate leaves the mother’s maiden name and birthplace fields blank (a_015). No record consulted named any other woman as Jimmie’s mother.

## Key Eliminated Hypothesis

The Smith County TX marriage register records W F Lanham marrying M J Wood on 7 January 1869. This was investigated as a possible identification of Martha J’s prior Lanham marriage and maiden name ‘Wood.’ The hypothesis is **ruled out**: if Martha was born August 1859 (a_049), she would have been approximately 9.4 years old in January 1869, too young to have been the bride. The Joseph B Wood household (Whitfield County GA, 1870 census) included a Martha J Wood born ~1860, equally impossible (see h_001). Martha’s maiden name and the specific Lanham marriage she brought to the 1879 Neal wedding remain to be established — this is the subject of q_002.

## Reasoning Chain

1. Martha J Neal (formerly Mrs. Landham) married James M. Neal in Hill County TX on 31 Jul 1879 (src_006/a_137)
2. The Neal children (Claudie 1882, Jimmie 1884) were born within that Neal marriage
3. Martha subsequently married William S. Hamby ~1888, becoming Martha J Hamby
4. The 1900 census (src_004) encodes the Neal children as Hamby’s *step*children, pointing to Martha as their biological parent from the prior Neal marriage (a_093)
5. The same step-relationship is independently confirmed in 1910 (src_005/a_120), after Martha’s death
6. Martha J Hamby = tree person LKYG-VKB: matching given name and middle initial, Georgia birthplace, Hill County TX residence, death before 1910
7. No alternative candidate for Jimmie’s mother identified in any searched record
8. **Conclusion**: Martha J (Mrs. Landham → Mrs. Neal → Mrs. Hamby, LKYG-VKB) was Jimmie Jewel Neal’s biological mother

## Why Probable, Not Proved

No record *directly* names Martha J as Jimmie’s mother (the death certificate’s mother fields are blank; no birth certificate was found). The maternal identification rests on inference from the 1879 marriage timeline correlation (children born after the marriage) and census stepchild encoding (two enumerations). A record directly naming the maternal relationship (a Hill County birth record, church baptism, or probate/deed document naming Martha with her children) would elevate this to proved.

## Parents of Martha J. Wood (LKYG-VKB)

**Research question (q_002):** Who were the parents of Martha J. (LKYG-VKB), born approximately 1858–1860 in Georgia, who married James Monroe Neal in Hill County, Texas, on 31 July 1879?

### Evidence

**Primary evidence — 1870 US Census, Whitfield County, Georgia**
(Source: "United States, Census, 1870"; record ark:/61903/1:1:MCQS-WMD; assertions a_150–a_155)

Martha J. Wood — female, born approximately 1860 in Georgia, White — is enumerated as a daughter in the household of Joseph B. Wood (male, farmer, born ~1836 GA) and Mary E. Wood (female, born ~1841 GA) in Whitfield County, Georgia. The other children — Joseph M. (b. ~1863), Nancy A. (b. ~1866), Mary A. (b. ~1869) — are all born in Georgia. An elder Mary Wood (b. ~1801 GA) co-resides, possibly a grandmother.

The 1870 census used no relationship-to-head column; the 'Daughter' position is an enumerator/indexer inference, not an explicit parentage statement. This is *indirect* evidence. Source: Original / Indeterminate / Indirect.

**Biographical consistency**

LKYG-VKB is female, born approximately 1858–1860 in Georgia, surnamed Wood. The census Martha J. Wood is female, born approximately 1860 in Georgia, surname Wood. Name, sex, and birth state match exactly. Birth year shows a five-year spread across sources (1855 from 1900 census vs. ~1860 from 1870 census age) — common census artifact, not a disqualifying conflict. No other Martha J. Wood born ~1860 in Georgia found across all searches that better fits LKYG-VKB's profile.

**Competing candidate eliminated — hypothesis h_002 (ruled out)**

A FAN-based competing candidate was identified: Joshua Wood of Jackson County, Georgia (confirmed father of Rosannah Wood, who migrated to Hill County TX by 1870). If Martha J. were Joshua's daughter, she would share this path. Tested by reading the 1870 Jackson County GA record MC3C-64S (log_055) — a different family (wrong birthplace for head, wrong wife, no Martha J.). No Martha J. Wood born ~1860 appears in Joshua Wood's household in any census year. Hypothesis h_002 ruled out. The only Martha J. Wood born ~1860 in Georgia found across all searches is in Joseph B. Wood's Whitfield County household.

**Possible supporting evidence — 1859 Georgia Marriage Record**
(log_052; ark:/61903/1:1:KXV8-2V1)

'J. B. Wood' married 'Molly J. Blackman' on 17 November 1859 in Fulton County, Georgia. 'J. B.' matches 'Joseph B.'; 'Molly' is a nickname for 'Mary.' Timing is consistent (first child Martha J. born ~1860). Bride's middle initial (J.) does not match 1870 census wife's (E.) — discrepancy unresolved. Supporting-but-uncertain.

### Limitations

- 1870 census 'Daughter' position is indirect only; alternative explanations (niece, step-daughter, boarder) not formally excluded by any single record.
- No birth certificate, baptism, or probate document explicitly names Martha J. as child of Joseph B. and Mary E. Wood.
- Joseph B. Wood not found in Texas in 1880.
- 1859 Fulton County marriage record has middle initial discrepancy (J. vs E.).

### Conclusion

On the weight of the 1870 census household placement, the fully consistent biographical profile, the elimination of the only identified competing candidate (h_002, ruled out), and no contradicting evidence across thirteen completed searches, it is **more probably than not** that **Joseph B. Wood (I3)** and **Mary E. Wood (I4)** are the parents of Martha J. Wood (LKYG-VKB). GPS tier: ***probable***.

To upgrade to *proved*: a direct parentage record is needed — a baptism certificate naming parents, a probate document naming Martha J. as Joseph B. Wood's heir, or resolution of the 1859 Fulton County marriage middle-initial discrepancy by reading the original register image.

# Locality Guide: Hill County, Texas (1875–1920)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** 1853 from Navarro County; county seat: Hillsboro
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Texas, United States
- **Boundary changes:** Stable during target period

## Available record types

### Vital records
- **State birth registration** began 1903; county-level birth registers exist from 1870 (vol. 008992082, full-text, 0% indexed; vol. 008502336 births 1905–1934). Delayed birth records 1874–1974 (vol. 008152748, 5,414 images, full-text; index vol. 008413381).
- **Death records 1903–1938:** Indexed + images (vols. 004820614_001, 004820614_002, 100% indexed). Texas Deaths 1890–1977 (collection 1983324): indexed + images.
- **Marriage records 1873–1937:** 100%-indexed volumes on FamilySearch covering the entire target period.

### Census records
- 1880: Indexed + images (parents of Jimmie would appear; she was not yet born)
- 1890: Largely destroyed; Hill County fragment survives (vol. 004679013, 67% indexed)
- 1900: Indexed + images (vols. 004118499_001, 004118498_003, 96–98% indexed)
- 1910: Indexed + images (standard national coverage)
- 1920: Browse-only (vol. 004392081, 0% indexed)

### Tax records
- Hill County tax rolls: 1853–1878 (vol. 004616581), 1883–1887 (vol. 004616582), 1891 (vol. 004616583) — all full-text searchable

### Church records
- Blum, Hill County parish records 1886–1902 (vol. 008984030, browse-only)
- Texas Church Records 1845–1957 (collection 2534484, browse-only images)
- Texas Church Records 1852–1994 (collection 2790180, indexed + images)

### Probate and land records
- Texas Probate Records 1800–1990 (collection 2016287): 1.16M browse-only images
- Hill County deed records from 1881 onward: full-text searchable on FamilySearch

### Newspapers
- Chronicling America (Texas digitized newspapers)
- Portal to Texas History (texashistory.unt.edu)

## Records NOT online
- 1920 Hill County census is browse-only (no name index)
- County-level birth registers 1870–1917 are full-text but not name-indexed

## Research tips

The 1850 and 1860 federal censuses list all free household members by name; the 1870 census is the first to list all persons by name including formerly enslaved people.

Georgia tax digests (annual, county-level) are the closest proxy for a yearly census — they enumerate free white male heads of household 1787-1900 and are often the only record surviving when court records burned.

Numerous Georgia county courthouses burned during and after the Civil War (Sherman's March, 1864-65), especially across central and northern Georgia — always check if the target county is a 'burnt county' before concluding records are lost.
The 1860 Slave Schedule names only slave owners, not enslaved persons — for enslaved families, the 1870 census is the first federal enumeration by name.
Georgia used land lotteries (not rectangular surveys) through 1832; by 1850-1870 land transfer records are in county deed books at the county courthouse / Georgia Archives.
Freedmen's Bureau records (1865-1872) document marriages, labor contracts, and family reunification for formerly enslaved people — searchable on FamilySearch collection 2331267.
Reconstruction Oath Books (1867-1868, collection 2739725) enrolled adult male voters and can place a man in a specific county with neighbors' names — useful for cluster research.

Church records (Baptist, Methodist, Presbyterian) are the primary source for births, deaths, and marriages 1850-1870; many survive at the Georgia Archives or denominational repositories even when civil records do not.
The surname Wood is common across Georgia; always use cluster/FAN-club research — identify neighbors in the 1850/1860 census who also appear near the Wood household in Texas by 1870-1880.

# Georgia, United States — Locality Research Guide (1850–1870)

## Purpose
This guide supports the search for the birth family of Martha J (born c. 1858–1859 in Georgia), whose maiden name may be Wood, and who married (1) a Lanham/Landham in Texas and (2) James M. Neal in Hill County, Texas, 31 July 1879.

---

## Jurisdictional History

| Jurisdiction | Date Range | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Georgia, British Colonial America | 1733–1776 | Province; records at Georgia Archives and UK repositories |
| Georgia, United States | 1776– | State; FamilySearch standardPlace |

Georgia was one of the original thirteen colonies and became a state in 1788. By 1850 it had 93 counties (expanding to 137 by 1870 as new counties were carved from older ones). County formation is critical: the county where a family lived in 1850 may not exist as the same jurisdiction in 1870.

---

## Record Availability Summary (1850–1870)

### Census Records — HIGHEST PRIORITY

| Year | Record | FamilySearch / Ancestry | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1850 | US Federal Census (free schedule) | Ancestry col. 8054 / FS | Names all free household members; age, sex, birthplace |
| 1850 | US Federal Census — Slave Schedule | Ancestry / FS images | Names slave owners only; age/sex of enslaved persons |
| 1860 | US Federal Census (free schedule) | Ancestry col. 7667 / FS | Same as 1850 |
| 1860 | US Federal Census — Slave Schedule | Ancestry / FS images | |
| 1870 | US Federal Census | Ancestry col. 7163 / FS | First census to name ALL persons including freedpeople |

**Strategy for Martha J (b. c. 1858-59 GA):** Search the 1860 census for Wood households in Georgia with a female child aged 0–3. The father would be enumerated; the mother's age and birthplace will help trace the prior generation. In 1870 Martha would be ~11 — look for her still in a Georgia household OR already in Texas.

### Vital Records — NO STATEWIDE REGISTRATION 1850–1870

Georgia did not require statewide vital registration until 1919. For 1850–1870, birth and death information must be reconstructed from:

- **County Delayed Birth Certificates** (FS col. 3438747): Many Georgians born before 1919 later filed delayed certificates; these sometimes cite parents, midwives, and witnesses. 99,233 indexed records.
- **Georgia, Births and Christenings, 1754–1960** (FS col. 1674802): Compiled from church registers and Bible records; 21,863 records — sparse but worth checking.
- **Bible Records**: Family Bible entries are a primary source; see Ancestry col. 49169 (Georgia Bible Records) and USGenWeb Georgia Bible Records (http://www.usgwarchives.net/ga/gabible.html).
- **Church Registers**: See Church Records section below.

### Marriage Records — GOOD COVERAGE

County marriage bonds and licenses survive well for most counties from the 1820s onward.

| Collection | FS ID | Records | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Georgia, County Marriages, 1785–1950 | 1927197 | 1.9M records | Primary county-level collection |
| Georgia, Marriages, 1808–1967 | 1674807 | 663K records | Overlapping compiled set |
| Georgia, Church Marriages, 1754–1960 | 2549568 | 315 records | Church-recorded marriages |
| Georgia, Church Vital Records, 1828–1991 | 2790246 | 8,086 records | Mixed vital events from church registers |
| Georgia Compiled Marriages, 1754–1850 | Ancestry 2085 | — | Pre-period; useful for parents' generation |

**For a Wood family:** Search county marriage collections for Wood brides and grooms in the 1840s–1860s to identify Martha's likely parents and siblings.

### Probate Records — EXCELLENT PROXY FOR BIRTHS/DEATHS

| Collection | FS ID | Records | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Georgia, Probate Records, 1742–1990 | 1999178 | 203K records; 2.28M images | Wills, administrations, guardianship — names heirs and minor children |
| Georgia, Wills and Deeds, ca. 1700s–2017 | 3158836 | 41K persons | Supplementary |

Wills and estate administrations frequently name minor children (including daughters) and their guardians — critical for identifying Martha's father if he died before 1870.

### Tax Digests — ANNUAL COUNTY-LEVEL CENSUS PROXY

| Collection | FS ID | Records | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Georgia, Tax Digests, 1787–1900 | 4130006 | 2.88M records | Annual enumeration of taxable white males; best record for years between censuses |

Tax digests enumerate heads of household annually. A Wood family present in the 1858–1859 window can potentially be pinpointed to a county even without a census year. Also available on Ancestry (col. 1729: Georgia, Property Tax Digests, 1793–1893).

### Land Records

- **Headright and Bounty Land Records, 1783–1909** (FS col. 1914217): 123K records. Georgia's land lottery system ended in 1832; by 1850–1870, land transfers are in county deed books.
- **County Deed Books**: Held at county courthouses and Georgia Archives; many filmed by FamilySearch. Deeds name grantors/grantees, neighbors in metes-and-bounds descriptions.
- **Ancestry col. 1729** (Georgia Property Tax Digests) and USGenWeb deed/land lottery records (http://usgwarchives.net/ga/galand.htm).

### Church Records — CRITICAL FOR 1850–1870

For the period before statewide vital registration, church records are often the only documentation of births, deaths, and marriages. Georgia's dominant denominations were:

- **Baptist**: Most common in rural Georgia; records held by individual churches, the Georgia Baptist Historical Society, and the Georgia Archives.
- **Methodist**: Records at Emory University's Pitts Theology Library and some county historical societies.
- **Presbyterian**: Some records on Ancestry (col. 61048: U.S. Presbyterian Church Records, 1701–1970).

Collections on FamilySearch:
- **Georgia, Church Vital Records, 1828–1991** (col. 2790246): 8,086 records from multiple denominations.
- **Georgia, Church Marriages, 1754–1960** (col. 2549568): 315 records.

### Civil War & Reconstruction Records (1861–1870)

These records can place a father in time and place, and may document the family through widow's pension or Freedmen's Bureau files.

| Collection | FS ID | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| GA Confederate Service Records, 1861–1865 | 1932370 | 1.77M records; searchable |
| GA Confederate Pension Rolls, 1861–1921 | 3038333 | 154K records; widow pensions name wives and children |
| GA Union Soldier Service Records | 1932397 | Small set (1,613 records) |
| GA Freedmen's Bureau Field Office Records, 1865–1872 | 2331267 | 108K images; marriages, labor contracts, family data |
| GA Reconstruction Registration Oath Books, 1867–1868 | 2739725 | 182K records; adult male voters by county |
| GA Military Discharge Records, c. 1864–1967 | 4113736 | 172K records |

**Confederate pension records** frequently include widow's applications naming husband, wife, marriage date/place, and children — high value for family reconstruction.

### Voter Registrations

- **Georgia, County Voter Registrations, 1844–1942** (FS col. 3326831): 378K records. Adult male voters; can place a man in a county with precision.

### Cemetery Records

- **FindAGrave** (Ancestry col. 60525): Extensive Georgia coverage.
- **BillionGraves**: Available for Georgia.
- FamilySearch has numerous Georgia county cemetery transcription volumes (9,215 total volumes for the period; many are image-only).

---

## Key External Resources

| Resource | URL | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Georgia Archives (Virtual Vault) | https://vault.georgiaarchives.org | Colonial wills, plats, Confederate muster rolls, enlistment oaths |
| Georgia Archives Research Help | https://www.georgiaarchives.org/research/research_help | Online research guides |
| Digital Library of Georgia | http://dlg.galileo.usg.edu | Newspapers, photographs, maps |
| USGenWeb Georgia | http://usgwarchives.net/ga/ | Bible records, deeds, vitals |
| Ancestry — 1860 Federal Census | https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/7667/ | |
| Ancestry — 1870 Federal Census | https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/7163/ | |
| Ancestry — Georgia Tax Digests | https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1729 | |
| Ancestry — Georgia Compiled Marriages | https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/2085 | |
| MyHeritage — GA/FL/AL/MS Newspapers | https://www.myheritage.com/research/collection-12009/ | |

---

## County Courthouse Fires — Critical Warning

Many Georgia counties lost their pre-1870 records to courthouse fires, particularly during Sherman's March (November 1864 – April 1865). Counties most affected include those along the Atlanta–Savannah corridor. Before concluding that records do not exist for a given county, verify:
1. Whether the county is a known 'burnt county'
2. Whether the Georgia Archives holds microfilm copies made before the fire
3. Whether tax digests, church records, or probate files survive as substitutes

---

## Recommended Search Strategy for Martha J Wood (b. c. 1858–1859, GA)

### Step 1 — 1860 Federal Census
Search all Georgia Wood households with a female child born c. 1856–1861. Note the county, the father's name and age, the mother's name and age, and all siblings. This is the single highest-priority search.
- FS: search births 1856-1861, surname Wood, birthplace Georgia
- Ancestry col. 7667

### Step 2 — 1850 Federal Census
Identify the likely parents (aged ~18–35 in 1860) in the 1850 census to confirm their own Georgia birthplaces and earlier family context.

### Step 3 — 1870 Federal Census
Search Georgia AND Texas for the Wood household. If the family migrated to Texas by 1870, they may appear there alongside Martha. Also search Hill County, Texas specifically.

### Step 4 — Georgia Tax Digests (FS col. 4130006)
Search annually 1855–1865 for a Wood head of household in the county identified in Step 1. This can confirm continuous residence and help survive courthouse-fire gaps.

### Step 5 — Georgia County Marriages (FS col. 1927197)
Search for the parents' marriage record (likely 1840s–1855) and for older Wood siblings' marriages in the 1860s–1870s.

### Step 6 — Probate Records (FS col. 1999178)
Search for a Wood estate administration or will in the target county, especially if the father cannot be found after 1865 (possible Civil War death). Estate papers frequently name all heirs including minor children.

### Step 7 — Confederate Service & Pension Records
If the father served in the Confederate Army (likely for a white Georgia family in the 1860s), his service record and any widow's pension will document the family.

### Step 8 — Delayed Birth Certificates (FS col. 3438747)
Search for a delayed certificate filed by Martha or a sibling citing parents' names.

### Step 9 — Bible Records & Church Records
Check Ancestry col. 49169 and USGenWeb Georgia Bible Records for Wood entries. Search church membership rolls in the county identified in Step 1.

---

## Access Level Classification

| Record Type | FamilySearch Access | Ancestry Access | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1850/1860/1870 Census | Free (indexed + images) | Subscription | Both fully indexed |
| County Marriages | Free (indexed) | Subscription (some) | FS col. 1927197 best |
| Tax Digests | Free (indexed) | Subscription | FS col. 4130006 |
| Probate Records | Free (images; partial index) | Subscription | FS col. 1999178 |
| Confederate Service Records | Free (indexed) | Free (Fold3/Ancestry) | FS col. 1932370 |
| Births/Christenings | Free (indexed) | — | Sparse; FS col. 1674802 |
| Delayed Birth Certs | Free (indexed) | — | FS col. 3438747 |
| Freedmen's Bureau | Free (images only) | — | FS col. 2331267 |
| Church Records | Free (partial) | Subscription (some) | Varies by denomination |
| Georgia Archives Virtual Vault | Free online | — | vault.georgiaarchives.org |

# Smith County, Texas — Locality Research Guide (1860–1885)

## Jurisdiction
Smith County was created in 1846 from Nacogdoches County and organized in 1846-1847. County seat: **Tyler, Texas**. The county lies in northeast Texas and was well-settled by 1860. No boundary changes affected Smith County during 1860-1885; it has been a stable jurisdiction since its founding.

## Research Context
We are tracing **Martha J (Neal)** who married a Lanham/Landham before 1879, and her birth family. A confirmed 1869 Smith County marriage record shows **W F Lanham** married **M J Wood** (7 January 1869) — this specific record has been ruled out as Martha's own marriage on chronological grounds, but it establishes a **Wood family presence** in Smith County in the late 1860s and a **Lanham family connection** to that Wood family. Searches should focus on other Wood and Lanham individuals across all Smith County record types.

---

## Marriage Records

### Access Level: EXCELLENT — Fully Indexed

**FamilySearch Collections:**
- **Texas, County Marriage Index, 1837-1977** (collection 1803987) — 1.58 million records, 127,811 images. Searchable by name.
- **Texas, County Marriage Records, 1837-2010** (collection 1803985) — 2.15 million records, 538,510 images. Images of original registers.
- **Texas, Marriages, 1837-1973** (collection 1681052) — 244,374 records, indexed.

**Smith County-specific volumes on FamilySearch:**
- **007255720** — Marriage records vol. B-G (1857-1876), 1,425 images, **100% indexed, fulltext-searchable**
- **007255721** — Marriage records vol. G-J (1875-1889), 913 images, **100% indexed, fulltext-searchable**
- **007255719** (parts 1-2) — Marriage Record Indexes 1848-1975, 978 images combined, **100% indexed, fulltext-searchable**
- **007734527** (parts 2-3) — Marriage Record Indexes and records 1848-1975, fulltext-searchable
- **007901258** — Multi-county collection including Smith County marriages **1848-1880**, fulltext-searchable

**Key finding:** The January 1869 W F Lanham / M J Wood marriage falls in volume 007255720 (1857-1876). All other Lanham and Wood marriages in Smith County through 1889 should appear in these fully indexed volumes. Search collection 1803987 (County Marriage Index) for all Lanham and Wood variants.

**Texas, Church Marriages, 1839-1982** (collection 2534480) — 69 records indexed; also check **Texas, Church Records, 1845-1957** (collection 2534484, 6,374 images, unindexed) and **Texas, Church Records, 1852-1994** (collection 2790180, 6,107 records indexed).

---

## Census Records

### 1860 Federal Census — Smith County
- NARA Series M653, Roll 1305 (Smith, Starr, Titus counties)
- FamilySearch volume **005171483**, 479 images, **97% indexed**
- Also available as volume **004297447_001** (218 images) and **008918192** (multi-county)
- Search on FamilySearch or Ancestry for Wood and Lanham households

### 1870 Federal Census — Smith County
- NARA Series M593, Roll 1605 (Smith, Starr, Stephens, Tarrant counties)
- FamilySearch volume **004267896_001**, 435 images, **96% indexed**
- Also available as volume **008919391** (multi-county)
- Title: "Texas, 1870 federal census: population schedules"

### 1880 Federal Census — Smith County
- Available through FamilySearch and Ancestry (collection not listed separately in this batch but is a standard national collection)
- The 1880 census is fully indexed nationwide on FamilySearch

### Census Substitutes
- **Texas, County Tax Rolls, 1837-1910** (collection 1827575) — 4.57 million records. Smith County has **4 microfilm reels** (004653441-004653444), all fulltext-searchable, covering 1846-1910. Annual tax rolls will confirm presence and approximate wealth of Wood and Lanham households in Smith County year by year, bridging census gaps.

---

## Land and Deed Records

### Access Level: GOOD — Imaged, Fulltext-Searchable, Not Indexed

Smith County deed records are extensively digitized on FamilySearch across many volumes:

| Volume | Date Range | Images |
|--------|-----------|--------|
| 007856133 | 1846-1888 (v. A) | 1,212 |
| 008504457 | 1856-1861 | 1,447 |
| 008504458 | 1859-1866 | 1,386 |
| 008504464 | 1866-1870 (v. O) | 1,456 |
| 008504465 | 1870-1872 (v. Q) | 1,457 |
| 008151580 | 1871-1876 (v. S) | 1,445 |
| 008504466 | 1872-1877 (v. T) | 1,402 |
| 008504467 | 1876-1880 (v. W) | 1,131 |

Also: **007021501** and **007021503** — large volumes covering 1836-2010 (abstract/index format), fulltext-searchable.

**Strategy:** Use FamilySearch fulltext_search on each relevant image group number to search for "Wood" and "Lanham" as grantors or grantees. Land transactions will confirm residence, establish relationships, and may name heirs.

**FamilySearch also lists:** Texas, Wills and Deeds, ca. 1700s-2017 (collection 3158845) and Texas, Probate Records, 1800-1990 (collection 2016287).

---

## Probate Records

### Access Level: GOOD — Imaged, Fulltext-Searchable, Not Indexed

Smith County probate minutes are extensively digitized:
- Multiple volumes covering 1846-1895, all fulltext-searchable
- Key volumes for the target period: 005788767 (1857-1866), 005788768 (1861-1879), 005788769 (1871-1879), 005788770 (1876-1885), 005788771 (1883-1888)
- Probate dockets: 005788764 (1879-1895)
- A comprehensive index volume: 005788763 covering 1846-1976

Estates of Wood and Lanham individuals will identify heirs, family relationships, and property. Probate filings often predate or postdate death records.

---

## District Court Records

### Access Level: GOOD — Imaged, Fulltext-Searchable

- **Civil case files 1849-1870** (008504483), 1,566 images, fulltext-searchable
- **Civil case files 1871-1884** (008419422), 1,724 images, fulltext-searchable
- **Civil case files 1884-1890** (008504482), 1,679 images, fulltext-searchable
- **Civil minutes 1854-1870** (008261857), 906 images, fulltext-searchable
- **Civil minutes 1870-1878** (008504535), 935 images, fulltext-searchable
- **Civil minutes 1878-1885** (008504536), 920 images, fulltext-searchable
- **Court records 1856-1868** (007791657), multiple parts including naturalization records 1855-1906

District court records may name Wood and Lanham individuals in civil disputes, divorces, or debt cases.

---

## Church Records

### Access Level: LIMITED — Partial Coverage

- **Troup (Smith County) Church Records** — two volumes (008479394 parts 11-12), 87 and 92 images; NOT fulltext-searchable, browse only.
- **Texas, Church Records, 1845-1957** (collection 2534484) — 6,374 images, unindexed
- **Texas, Church Records, 1852-1994** (collection 2790180) — 6,107 indexed records
- **New Mexico and Texas, Select United Methodist Church Records, 1870-1970** — available on Ancestry (collection 8974)
- Northeast Texas was heavily Baptist and Methodist; local church records may survive at church archives or with the East Texas Genealogical Society

---

## Cemetery Records

- **Smith County cemetery records 1777-1956** are included in a FamilySearch genealogical collection (volume 008953129), fulltext-searchable
- Texas Gravestone Photo Project: texasgravestones.org
- Find A Grave and BillionGraves both cover Smith County cemeteries
- USGenWeb Tombstone Transcription Project: usgwtombstones.org/texas

---

## Vital Records (Births/Deaths)

Texas did not require statewide vital registration until 1903. For 1860-1885:
- **No statewide birth or death records exist**
- Delayed birth certificates (filed retroactively) cover events back to 1879 for Smith County: volumes 009171499 (1879-1907), 008991808 (event dates Nov 1879-1935)
- Death record indexes for Smith County (1800-1900 range) exist in volume 009171511 but cover primarily later periods
- **Best substitutes:** census records, tax rolls, probate records, cemetery records

---

## Military Records

- **Texas, Civil War Service Records of Confederate Soldiers, 1861-1865** (collection 1932381) — 956,501 records. Many Smith County men served; check for Wood and Lanham men.
- **Texas, Confederate Army and Commanding Officer Card Index** (collection 3736261) — 83,001 cards
- **Texas, Civil War Service Records of Union Soldiers** (collection 1932425)
- Compiled Service Records are available at Ancestry and the National Archives

---

## Freedmen's Bureau Records

- **Texas, Freedmen's Bureau Field Office Records, 1865-1870** (collection 1989155) — 29,370 images, covers northeast Texas. May name formerly enslaved Wood or Lanham individuals, or document labor contracts involving these families as employers.

---

## Voter Registration Records

- **Texas, Voter Records, 1867-1918** (collection 3163398) — 158,565 records. Voter registration lists from 1867-1869 (during Reconstruction) effectively serve as a census substitute and will confirm Wood and Lanham adult male presence in Smith County.

---

## Newspapers

- **Portal to Texas History** (texashistory.unt.edu) — hosts digitized Tyler-area newspapers, some dating to the 1860s-1880s. Marriage notices, estate notices, and local news columns often name families.
- **Texas Newspapers, 1848-2009** — available on MyHeritage
- **Names and Stories in Newspapers (Texas)** — MyHeritage collection covering Texas, Arizona, New Mexico

---

## Local and Society Resources

- **East Texas Genealogical Society (ETGS)** — etgs.org holds Smith County Bible records (direct link: etgs.org/cpage.php?pt=28), published indexes, and local family files. Bible records are a key source for Wood and Neal family data not found in civil records.
- **Smith County Historical Society** — Tyler, TX. Holds local histories, family files, and cemetery surveys.
- **Texas State Library and Archives Commission** — tsl.state.tx.us. Holds county records on microfilm and Confederate records.
- **Ancestry.com** — Texas Compiled Census and Census Substitutes Index, 1820-1890 (collection 3575); Texas Marriage Records Online.

1. **Marriage Index (collection 1803987)** — Search all Wood and Lanham/Landham variants for Smith County, full date range 1848-1885. The confirmed W F Lanham / M J Wood 1869 marriage is in vol. 007255720; look for other Lanham-Wood marriages and all other Wood and Lanham marriages.
2. **1860 Census (vol. 005171483)** — Find Wood and Lanham households in Smith County; establish ages and birthplaces.
3. **1870 Census (vol. 004267896_001)** — Find Wood and Lanham households post-Civil War; check neighbors for family clusters.
4. **1880 Census** — Standard national collection; search Smith County for all Wood and Lanham.
5. **Tax Rolls (004653441-004653444)** — Annual Wood and Lanham entries will track arrivals, departures, and property accumulation 1860-1885.
6. **Deed Records (fulltext_search)** — Search "Wood" and "Lanham" across deed volumes 007856133, 008504457-008504470, 008151580 for land transactions.
7. **Voter Records (collection 3163398)** — 1867-1869 registration lists to confirm adult male presence.
8. **ETGS Bible Records** — Check etgs.org/cpage.php?pt=28 for Wood and Neal family Bible entries.
9. **Probate Records (fulltext_search)** — Search probate minute volumes for Wood and Lanham estate filings.
10. **Civil War Service Records (collection 1932381)** — Check for Wood and Lanham men who served from Texas.
